trellis_budget.selection_policy: visual inspection first; hold remaining Trellis slots for later image batches unless a current candidate is clearly superior
trellis_budget.spent_or_queued_runs: 5 selected candidates; 1 source-native route failed before work, 4 bad-cwd submissions failed before work, 1 memory-incident stale recovery, 1 safety cancellation, 5 completed Trellis casts preserved.

trellis_casts.visual_verdict: Coherent dark turtle/crab-like armored creature-object; preserves shell bulk, planted feet, green foot-moss, and orange internal glints, but lighting/style are too dark for final aesthetic judgment.
Strong good-miss cast: turtle-shaped armored relic with citadel/tower dorsal forms, heavy feet, red-orange ports, and coherent 3D objectness.
Coherent quadruped walker with box carapace, orange ocular/emissive ports, mechanical legs, and green overgrowth; long runtime but basin survives into mesh strongly.

First scaffold-to-creature cast hit: coherent segmented grub/worm body with armor bands, spikes, small feet, orange semantic/sensory spots, and a tube-mouth structure; too toy-armored for final LIRMS but identity survives around the form.
Strongest LIRM proof: continuous worm/grub body, mouth-at-front, segmented belly, stumpy limbs, armor plates, spines/bumps, and side-view identity survival from crude armature conditioning.

trellis_route_verdict.memory_incident_read: One earlier LIRM decode job failed during the box memory incident, but both LIRM requeues completed cleanly in about 170s each through GPU Greenroom; current evidence points to contention/unified-memory pressure, not Trellis being intrinsically box-killing.
trellis_route_verdict.next_slice_default: Improve morphology armature controls and prompts toward less toy-armored, more LIRMS-native grub/worm bodies, then rerun a small image/Trellis matrix with Blender witnesses.
trellis_route_verdict.summary: Flux2 basin outputs and crude LIRM armature controls survived Trellis into coherent mesh/texture casts. LIRM24 proves the scaffold-to-image-to-Trellis route can preserve creature identity strongly enough to justify a dedicated morphology-armature iteration slice.

takeaways: Pixal3D object sources are strong basin scaffolds for Flux2 style/identity shifts.
Insertion prompts can add coherent molten/orb/relic objects into landscape and interior scenes instead of merely pasting symbols.
Good-miss creature/object basins are real: p3d06_crab_orange_walker_relic keeps source posture while inventing production-like body detail.
p3d00_turtle_style_clay_maquette is a low-risk Trellis candidate, held pending LIRM armature outputs.
The crude 3D armature conditioning is effective: axial curve, segmenting, head/mouth direction, contact posture, and orange semantic spots survive into imagegen outputs.
Clay inputs produce more toy/maquette creature bodies; normal inputs produce stranger but still posture-bound variants.
This is the desired good-miss regime: the generator fills surface structure while the armature controls body plan.

visual_observations.decision: Final Trellis slots correctly assigned to lirm16 clay and lirm24 normal rather than additional Pixal3D style outputs.
strongest_basins: LIRM armature good-miss: all eight crude 3D controls produce coherent segmented creature variants, with body-plan preservation visible.
Dark-orange miniature architecture: house/tower/oracle variants are aesthetically coherent and object/scene stable.
Bounded scene insertion: island shrine, underwater ruin, room reactor, and plant/tree object insertions add objects without destroying source composition.
Mechanical creature/object transforms: turtle and crab variants preserve posture/objectness while mutating material identity.
weak_or_secondary_basins: Some style transfers become illustration-like rather than mesh-friendly assets.
Plant/metal hybrids are visually strong but may be hostile for Trellis because of thin leaves/ribs and mixed scene/object boundaries.
Mask/bust late outputs are isolated and interesting, but less relevant to current creature-control question.
